description: The Advanced Himawari Imager (AHI) flight model AHI-09 on Himawari-9, a 16-band imager from the visible and shortwave infrared to the thermal infrared (0.47-13.3 um) for JMA's geostationary meteorological mission. The curves are the band relative spectral responsivities released by JMA (October 2013, provided by ITT Exelis); each is the whole-instrument band response, peak 1.
facility_description: Himawari-8 and Himawari-9 are Japan Meteorological Agency geostationary meteorological satellites carrying the Advanced Himawari Imager, which succeeded the imagers of the MTSAT series.

Band01.DetectorType_note: SVO's Himawari/AHI9.Band01 array is not archived here; its record labels the band photon. JMA's workbook column is 'Relative Responsivity [-]' and JMA states no photon/energy convention for it; its GSICS page says only that 'The Planck function and sensor spectral response functions are used to compute brightness temperature [K] from radiance [mW.m-2.sr-1.cm] and vice-versa' (https://www.data.jma.go.jp/mscweb/data/monitoring/gsics/ir/techinfo_geoleoir.html), which weights radiance (the energy form). NOAA states the energy form explicitly for the analogous VIIRS RSRs (ATBD 474-00027 Eq. 9) and GOES-R ABI SRFs (doi:10.1117/12.2238090 Eq. 1-2), but no JMA document found says it for AHI, so NJM's energy stays assumed.

notes: Description and facility text paraphrase https://www.data.jma.go.jp/mscweb/en/himawari89/space_segment/spsg_ahi.html: 'Himawari-8 and Himawari-9 have a new payload called the Advanced Himawari Imager (AHI) for dedicated meteorological mission ... The functions and specifications are notably improved from those of the imagers on board MTSATs'. Satellite mapping from the workbook header 'Flight Model: AHI-09', the workbook Title note 'Advance Himawari Imager (AHI-9) on Himawari-9', and SVO's archived Himawari/AHI9 records (Facility 'Himawari-9'). The page credits the SRF files as 'provided by ITT Exelis'; JMA's terms say third-party rights may apply where indicated, and no restriction is stated for these files. The workbook's Title sheet keeps an older note calling the SRFs 'estimated' and 'cited from the document AHI-12-177' with 'tentative' central wavelengths, followed by a newer note that 'The center wavelengths have been updated to match these curves.' Photon/energy weighting is not stated by the owner; the staged DetectorType=energy is tagged 'assumed' (SVO uses DetectorType 1, photon counter, for these IDs; pivots differ by <=0.16 %).
